description.value: The study investigated sex differences in cognitive regulation of psychosocial achievement stress using functional MRI in healthy females and males.

spans.text: This study used functional magnetic resonance imaging in 23 females and 20 males to investigate cognitive downregulation of negative, stressful sensations during a frequently used psychosocial stress task.

value: the application of a cognitive regulation strategy leads to less subjective stress experience in both sexes
Using cognitive regulation during stress will affect the psychophysiological responses differently in females and males and furthermore prompt sex differences in neural activation.

spans.text: we hypothesized that the application of a cognitive regulation strategy leads to less subjective stress experience in both sexes.

description.value: The study included healthy female and male volunteers in a repeated-measures psychosocial stress experiment with nonregulation and regulation blocks.

description.value: A verbal intelligence neuropsychological test was administered to control for potential group differences in neurocognitive abilities.
The Trail-Making Test, parts A and B, was administered to assess executive functions.
A digit span test was administered to assess working memory.
The German version of the coping inventory for stressful situations was administered to assess stress coping.
The German version of the emotion regulation questionnaire was administered to assess emotion regulation strategies.
The FPI-R was administered to assess personality characteristics.
The BDI 2 was administered to assess depression.
The STAI was administered to assess anxiety ratings.

description.value: Participants performed mental arithmetic tasks for 70 seconds with an adaptive time limit based on previous performance and negative social comparison/performance feedback; the design targeted 45–55% correct responses.

spans.text: In the stress condition, additionally, a time limit is enforced for each task, depending on the participant's previous performance.

instructions.value: In the nonregulation block, perform the mental arithmetic task normally and treat performance as important for subsequent data analysis. In the regulation block, regulate negative sensations in a top-down attentional manner by suppressing negative sensations, placing less emphasis on the time limit and negative performance feedback, and focusing on intrinsic motivation to improve performance while remaining motivationally involved.

spans.text: For the second block (regulation), participants were instructed to regulate their negative sensations in a top‐down attentional manner.
